title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck works in GL(2,Ẑ) with two automorphisms of finite order:
- ρ, of order 3, given by conjugation by the order-3 element of SL(2,Z);
- σ_∞, of order 2, the involution attached to the elliptic point of order 2.
The unknowns are a pair (α, β) of matrices, as in (63). He writes
- ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} = (A B; C D),
- η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} = (R S; T U),
with det α = δ = ε_3 ∈ {±1} and det β = 1. The explicit formulas (66) and (68) are given on the previous page. The 'relation des lacets' (69) reads ξ = ε·η·(1 0; 2ν 1), with ε = ±1 and ν ∈ Ẑ.

This is the linearised (GL_2-valued) form of a loop / hexagon-type equation. It parallels the GT-type relation in which λ = 2m+1. Here μ = 2ν+1 plays the role of λ, and the matrices α, β play the role of the conjugating elements (the 'f' of Drinfeld/Ihara) projected to GL_2. So the page is solving the abelianised/linear shadow of the loop equation for the modular group PSL2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3. This is part of the 'Longue Marche' programme of describing the Galois/Teichmüller action on the tower of modular curves.

Step (70). Determinants: AD − BC = 1 and RU − ST = 1.

Step (71). From (66): δ(C + D − B) = ad − bc = δ, hence C + D − B = 1. From (68), T = S.

Step (72). Expanding (69) entrywise gives
- A = ε(R + 2νS),
- B = εS,
- C = ε(T + 2νU),
- D = εU.
Using T = S, the C-equation becomes C = B + 2νD. Combined with (71), this gives (2ν+1)D = 1, i.e. μD = 1. A is then forced by the determinant. So (69) is equivalent to the boxed system D = εU, μD = 1, B = εS. In particular μ is a unit of Ẑ.

Step (73). Substituting (66) and (68): c² + cd + d² = δD = δ/μ, and the B-equation becomes ac + bd + bc = δεS.

Step (74). Arithmetic consequences:
- Since c² + cd + d² ≡ (c − d)² mod 3 and δ/μ is a unit, we get δ/μ ≡ 1 mod 3, i.e. δ ≡ μ (3).
- From U = t² + u² = εD = ε/μ, which is a unit (odd) and a sum of two squares, we get t² + u² ≡ 1 mod 4, i.e. ε ≡ μ (4).

Step (75). Hence the signs are the quadratic characters of conductor 3 and 4 evaluated at μ: δ = ε_3(μ) = (−3/μ) and ε = ε_2(μ) = (−1)^{(μ−1)/2}. These are the characters attached to Q(√−3) and Q(i), i.e. to the elliptic points j = 0 and j = 1728 of orders 3 and 2.

The page then announces that formula (83) of p. 370 simplifies here. On the next page this becomes (76): δα(cρ + d) = β(tσ_∞ + u)τ_∞^{a_2}, which reduces to D = εU, B = εS. That leads to the definition of the upper-triangular element u_{α,β} = (μ μB; 0 1).
errors: In (73) the δ factors are omitted. From (66), c²+cd+d² = δD and ac+bd+bc = δB, so the correct relations are c²+cd+d² = δε(t²+u²) = δ/μ and ac+bd+bc = δε(rt+su). As literally written, ε(t²+u²) = δ/μ would give εδ ≡ μ (4) rather than ε ≡ μ (4). The stated conclusion (74) is the correct one, consistent with D = εU and μD = 1.
(71): the right-hand relation should read T − S = 0, i.e. T = S. This is immediate from (68), where S = T = rt+su; it is not 'T − S = 1'.

ideas.what: Reduction of the GL2(Ẑ)-linearised loop relation ξ = ε·η·(1 0; 2ν 1) (with ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1}) to the system D = εU, B = εS, μD = 1, with μ = 2ν+1
ideas.modern_name: abelianised/linear (GL_2) image of the GT-type hexagon relation for Γ(1) = PSL2(Z) ≅ Z/2*Z/3, with λ = 2m+1
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT relations: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; GT acting on the modular group / Γ_{1,1}: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997), Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and modular group only programmatically; this computation is unpublished

ideas.what: The signs in the loop relation are forced to be the conductor-3 and conductor-4 quadratic characters of the 'cyclotomic' parameter μ: δ = ε_3(μ), ε = ε_2(μ), via c²+cd+d² ≡ square mod 3 and sum of two squares ≡ 1 mod 4
ideas.modern_name: characters χ_{-3}, χ_{-4} attached to the elliptic points j=0, j=1728 (CM by Q(√−3), Q(i)) in the Galois action on π1 of M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; such characters appear in Nakamura's and Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps' explicit formulas for Galois/GT action on π1(M_{1,1})

missed.claim: In the GL2(Ẑ) shadow of the loop equation, the two sign ambiguities are canonically the quadratic characters of conductor 3 and 4 of the parameter μ = 2ν+1. This explicitly ties the orders 3 and 2 of the elliptic points to the arithmetic of Q(√−3) and Q(i) inside a GT-type equation. The connection is plausibly known implicitly in work on GT and Γ_{1,1}, but this specific elementary derivation is a nice unpublished detail.
missed.quote: δ ≡ μ (3), ε ≡ μ (4) qui caractérisent les signes δ, ε comme δ = ε_3(μ) = ε_3, ε = ε_2(μ) = ε_2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an explicit normalisation of signs for the action of GT-like groups on the profinite modular group. That could be relevant to comparisons with the Galois action on π1(M_{1,1}) at the elliptic points.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out elementary but careful matrix algebra reducing a linearised loop equation, ending with a neat identification of the signs as conductor-3 and conductor-4 characters. Nicely done, but expected, and close in spirit to known GT/modular-group results.
transcription_corrections: (71) right side: 'T − S = 0 i.e. T = S' (machine reading '=1' is likely wrong; the image shows 'T = S = 1' struck/ambiguous, but the mathematics requires T = S).
(73) third line is struck out: 'μ(c²+cd+d²) = δ'.
Line after (73): 'C'est des deux premières relations (73) que l'on tire aussitôt'.
Last lines: '(valable sans conditions autres que celles précisées jusqu'ici sur α, β, f — f n'intervenant d'ailleurs pas pour le moment dans la formulation)'.
